newMuslims.shahadaTitle: How to Become a Muslim — The Shahada
newMuslims.shahadaIntro: Becoming a Muslim is simple. You enter Islam by sincerely declaring the Shahada — the testimony of faith. No certificate, ceremony, or permission from anyone is required. Allah accepts you the moment your heart submits.
newMuslims.shahadaArabic: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّٰهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّٰهِ
newMuslims.shahadaTransliteration: Ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan rasulullah
newMuslims.shahadaMeaning: I bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.
newMuslims.shahadaCtaText: Want to take this step with someone walking beside you? We are here.
newMuslims.norwayTitle: Your First Steps as a Muslim in Norway
newMuslims.norwayIntro: Dawah Norway has teams in six cities — Oslo, Trondheim, Stavanger, Kristiansand, Tromsø and Østfold — ready to support you with mosque connections, free Qurans and one-to-one mentorship in Norwegian or English.
newMuslims.norwayStep1: Take a ritual bath (ghusl) and learn how to perform wudu before prayer.
newMuslims.norwayStep2: Find your nearest mosque for Friday prayer and ask us if you need help locating one.
newMuslims.norwayStep3: Order a free Quran in English or Norwegian via our contact form — we ship anywhere in Norway.
newMuslims.norwayStep4: Connect with a mentor who can answer questions in your language as you learn the prayer and the basics of the faith.
newMuslims.faqQ1: How do I become a Muslim in Norway?
newMuslims.faqA1: You become a Muslim by sincerely declaring the Shahada (above). No certificate or permission is required, but we recommend reaching out for guidance and community.
newMuslims.faqQ2: Do I have to change my name?
newMuslims.faqA2: No. Islam does not require you to change your name unless its meaning contradicts Islamic belief. Most converts keep their existing name.
newMuslims.faqQ3: What do I do after taking the Shahada?
newMuslims.faqA3: Take a ritual bath (ghusl), learn wudu and the five daily prayers. We offer one-to-one guidance, a free Quran, and a mentor.
newMuslims.faqQ4: Where can I find a mosque in Norway?
newMuslims.faqA4: There are mosques in Oslo, Trondheim, Stavanger, Kristiansand, Tromsø and Østfold. Email info@dawahnorway.com and we will help you find the nearest one.
newMuslims.faqQ5: Can I get a free Quran?
newMuslims.faqA5: Yes — we distribute free Qurans across Norway. Use the contact form or email info@dawahnorway.com.

about.title: About Us
about.bismillah: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
about.intro: Dawah Norway is a non-profit organization founded in 2021 in Norway, dedicated to educating both Muslim and non-Muslim communities about Islam through information tables, dawah stands, and organized classes.
about.historyText: Founded in 2021, Dawah Norway has grown into an active community inviting people to Islam with wisdom and compassion. We adhere to the Qur'an and authentic Sunnah, following the 'Aqidah of Ahlus-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah. With six local teams across Norway — in Oslo, Østfold, Kristiansand, Stavanger, Trondheim, and Tromsø — we actively work to share the message of Islam.
about.quranVerse: Let there be a group among you who call others to goodness, encourage what is good, and forbid what is evil — it is they who will be successful.

whyIslam.title: Why Islam?
whyIslam.intro: Islam is the universal message of submission to the One God. Here are key reasons why millions embrace this timeless faith.
whyIslam.s1Text: Islam emphasizes a personal bond with God. This connection encourages believers to maintain constant awareness of the divine, forming the foundation of lasting happiness. The faith teaches that peace originates from God, and through nurturing this relationship and following divine guidance, believers achieve inner peace.
whyIslam.s1Quote: Truly, in remembering God do hearts find rest.
whyIslam.s2Text: Islam provides perspective by viewing life's events as divine tests. Believers are encouraged to interpret occurrences within life's broader purpose: acknowledging and obeying God. The faith advocates focusing on controllable aspects, expressing gratitude for blessings, and practicing patience during hardship — creating contentment and preventing life's extremes.
whyIslam.s3Title: Pure and Clear Concept of God
whyIslam.s3Text: Islam emphasizes God's absolute perfection and uniqueness. God is singular, without partners or equals, and solely worthy of worship. The faith stresses divine power, perfection, and supreme nature across all realms.
whyIslam.s4Text: Islam encourages using intellect to contemplate existence and the cosmos. The Quran serves as proof of divine origin through its preservation, universal message, linguistic beauty, and scientific foreknowledge.
whyIslam.s5Text: Islam balances hope in divine mercy with fear of judgment. Humans possess autonomy to err but can seek forgiveness through sincere repentance, which strengthens their bond with God without requiring intermediaries.
whyIslam.s6Text: Every individual faces accountability for their actions. The Day of Judgment ensures equitable retribution and divine justice, nurturing harmonious societies grounded in fairness.
whyIslam.s7Title: Practical and Balanced Way of Life
whyIslam.s7Text: Islam harmonizes belief with action, addressing spiritual, physical, psychological, and societal needs. Daily prayers and annual fasting provide purpose, humility, and community connection.
whyIslam.s8Text: Islam's message applies to all humanity across ages, inviting personal spiritual journeys based on faith and righteousness rather than earthly distinctions.

muhammad.title: Who is Muhammad ﷺ?
muhammad.intro: Muslims regard Muhammad (peace be upon him) as the final Prophet in a succession that includes Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, David, Solomon, and Jesus. His life is the living embodiment of the Qur'an.
muhammad.aishaQuote: His character was a reflection of the Quran.
muhammad.missionText: Muhammad ﷺ emphasized that authentic faith manifests through righteous conduct and compassionate treatment. He taught that the best of people are those with the best character, and stressed mercy toward all.
muhammad.missionQuote: And We have not sent you (Muhammad) except as a mercy for mankind.
muhammad.forgivenessText: Muhammad ﷺ exemplified extreme patience and forgiveness, particularly when possessing power to retaliate.
muhammad.forgivenessQuote: Keep to forgiveness (O Muhammad), and enjoin kindness, and turn away from the ignorant.
muhammad.equalityText: He taught universal human equality — that no race, color or status raises one above another; only piety does.
muhammad.equalityQuote: All humanity is from Adam, and Adam is from clay. There is no superiority for an Arab over a non-Arab, nor for a black over a white, except through piety.
muhammad.toleranceText: Muhammad ﷺ taught self-control in the face of provocation.
muhammad.toleranceQuote: The strong is not the one who overcomes people by his strength, but the strong is the one who controls himself while in anger.
muhammad.gentlenessText: A ten-year companion noted his consistent gentleness. He advised his wife that gentleness beautifies everything it touches.
muhammad.humblenessText: He refused special treatment, sitting wherever space permitted and mixing with the poor. He cautioned against excessive praise, reminding his followers that he was only the Lord's servant.
muhammad.husbandText: He encouraged companions to emulate his example in family life, saying the most perfect believers are the best in morals — and the best among them are those who are best to their wives.
muhammad.gandhiQuote: It was the rigid simplicity, the utter self-effacement of the Prophet, the scrupulous regard for his pledges, his intense devotion to his friends and followers, his intrepidity, his fearlessness, his absolute trust in God and in his own mission. These and not the sword carried everything before them and surmounted every obstacle.
muhammad.shawQuote: The world is in dire need of a man with the mind of Muhammad. I came to the conclusion that he was never an enemy of Christianity, and must be called instead the saviour of humanity.
muhammad.exploreWhyIslamText: Eight reasons people embrace Islam — from a clear understanding of God to a balanced way of life.

muhammad.faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions About Muhammad ﷺ
muhammad.faqA1: Muhammad ﷺ (c. 570–632 CE) is regarded by Muslims as the final prophet of God, sent to all of humanity. Muslims believe he received the Quran over 23 years and lived as a model of mercy, justice and devotion, in a line of prophets including Adam, Abraham, Moses and Jesus.
muhammad.faqQ2: When and where was Muhammad ﷺ born?
muhammad.faqA2: Muhammad ﷺ was born around 570 CE in Mecca, in present-day Saudi Arabia. Raised an orphan, he became known for his honesty and was given the title Al-Amin (the trustworthy) before receiving prophethood at the age of forty.
muhammad.faqA3: No. Muslims do not worship Muhammad ﷺ. Worship in Islam is directed to God (Allah) alone. Muhammad ﷺ is honoured and followed as Gods messenger and the best example of how to live, but he is a human being, not divine.
muhammad.faqQ4: What is the Sunnah of Muhammad ﷺ?
muhammad.faqA4: The Sunnah is the recorded sayings, actions and approvals of Muhammad ﷺ. Alongside the Quran, it is a primary source of guidance in Islam, showing Muslims how to pray, treat others, and live with character and balance.
muhammad.faqQ5: Why do Muslims say peace be upon him (ﷺ)?
muhammad.faqA5: When Muslims mention Muhammad ﷺ they add peace be upon him (in Arabic, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, shown by the symbol ﷺ) as a sign of love and respect, following an instruction in the Quran to honour the Prophet.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Dawah Norway is committed to protecting your privacy. This policy explains what information we collect, how we use it, and the rights you have.
privacy.collectText: We collect information you voluntarily share with us through our contact form (name, email, country, message, and optional phone number) and basic technical data (IP address, browser type) for security purposes.
privacy.useText: We use your information only to respond to your inquiries, support your journey with Islamic resources, and improve the quality of our outreach. We never sell or share your data with third parties for marketing.
privacy.donationsText: When you donate via Vipps, Stripe, or PayPal, we receive limited transaction information from the provider — your name, the donated amount, and a reference ID. We do not receive or store card numbers or full payment details. For recurring donations via Vipps, we additionally receive an agreement ID required to manage the subscription. Donation records are retained for 5 years after the end of the financial year, as required by the Norwegian Bookkeeping Act (§ 13). Vipps MobilePay AS, Stripe, Inc., and PayPal each act as independent data controllers for the payment data they process — see their respective privacy policies for details.
privacy.cookiesText: We use essential cookies required for the site to function and optional analytics cookies that help us understand how the site is used. You can control cookie preferences at any time.
privacy.rightsText: You have the right to access, correct, or delete the personal information we hold about you. To exercise these rights, contact us at info@dawahnorway.com. If you believe we are processing your personal data unlawfully, you may complain to the Norwegian Data Protection Authority (Datatilsynet — postkasse@datatilsynet.no, www.datatilsynet.no).
privacy.contactText: For any questions about this privacy policy, reach out to info@dawahnorway.com or call +47 489 20 006.

freeQuran.title: Free Quran — Order Your Free Copy
freeQuran.intro: The Quran is the word of God, a guidance for all mankind. We distribute free Quran copies across Norway.
freeQuran.heroTitle: The Quran — Guidance for All Mankind
freeQuran.heroText: The Holy Quran is the final revelation of God to humanity, revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ over 23 years. It is a complete guide for life — addressing faith, morality, worship, and the purpose of existence.
freeQuran.quoteArabic: ذَٰلِكَ الْكِتَابُ لَا رَيْبَ ۛ فِيهِ ۛ هُدًى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
freeQuran.quoteText: This is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guidance for those conscious of God.
freeQuran.aboutText: The Quran is the literal word of God (Allah), preserved in its original Arabic text for over 1,400 years without any change. It was revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through the Angel Jibreel (Gabriel). The Quran is the foundation of Islamic faith and covers every dimension of human life — from personal conduct and family life to ethics, spirituality, and the relationship between humanity and its Creator.
freeQuran.reason1Text: Unlike any other religious text, the Quran claims to be the direct, literal speech of God — unchanged since its revelation. For over 1,400 years, it has been memorized word-for-word by millions.
freeQuran.reason2Text: The Quran addresses the deepest questions of human existence: Who created us? Why are we here? What happens after death? It provides clear, practical guidance for every aspect of life.
freeQuran.reason3Text: The Quran challenged the greatest poets and linguists of Arabia — and continues to challenge the world — to produce even one chapter like it. Its inimitable style remains unmatched 14 centuries later.
freeQuran.reason4Text: The Quran is not for a specific people, place, or time. Its message is for all of humanity — addressing people of every background with wisdom and mercy.
freeQuran.orderText: Dawah Norway distributes free copies of the Quran across Norway in Norwegian, English, Arabic and other languages. We ship anywhere in Norway at no cost.
freeQuran.gratiskoranText: You can also order a free Quran directly through our dedicated service. Free shipping across all of Norway.
freeQuran.faqQ1: Is the Quran available in Norwegian?
freeQuran.faqA1: Yes. We have Norwegian-language Qurans available. Order through our contact form or visit gratiskoran.no.
freeQuran.faqA2: Yes — completely free. We cover printing and shipping costs through donations. There is no obligation whatsoever.
freeQuran.faqA3: Usually 3–7 business days anywhere in Norway. For urgent requests, contact us directly.
freeQuran.faqQ4: Can I get Qurans for a group or school?
freeQuran.faqA4: Yes. We supply bulk orders for groups, schools, and communities. Contact us with the quantity and we will arrange delivery.

whatIsIslam.title: What is Islam?
whatIsIslam.intro: Islam is the faith of roughly two billion people worldwide. The word 'Islam' means peace through willing submission to God. A Muslim is anyone who submits to God — the one Creator, known in Arabic as Allah. Islam teaches that God sent prophets throughout history, from Adam to Muhammad ﷺ, all carrying the same core message: worship the one God and live with justice and mercy.
whatIsIslam.meaningText: 'Islam' comes from the Arabic root s-l-m, which carries the meanings of peace, safety and submission. To be Muslim is to find inner peace by aligning your life with the will of the Creator. The religion is not named after a person or a place, but after this relationship between the human being and God.
whatIsIslam.godText: The foundation of Islam is tawhid — the belief that there is only one God, with no partners, no children and nothing comparable to Him. God is the Creator and Sustainer of everything, all-knowing and all-merciful. Muslims worship God directly, without intermediaries, idols or images.
whatIsIslam.quranText: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. Muslims believe it is the literal word of God, revealed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ over 23 years and preserved unchanged in its original Arabic for over 1,400 years. It guides Muslims in belief, worship, character and daily life.
whatIsIslam.prophetText: Muhammad ﷺ (c. 570–632 CE) is the final prophet in Islam, sent to all of humanity. Muslims do not worship him; they honour him as God's messenger and the best example of how to live. He stands in a long line of prophets that includes Abraham, Moses and Jesus.
whatIsIslam.pillarsText: Islam is built on five pillars: the declaration of faith (Shahada), prayer (Salah), giving to charity (Zakat), fasting in Ramadan (Sawm) and pilgrimage to Mecca (Hajj). Together they shape a balanced life of devotion, generosity and self-discipline.
whatIsIslam.norwayText: Islam is one of the largest religions in Norway, with communities and mosques in Oslo, Trondheim, Stavanger, Kristiansand, Tromsø and beyond. Dawah Norway helps both Muslims and non-Muslims learn about Islam through free Qurans, lectures and one-to-one mentorship across the country.
whatIsIslam.ctaText: Want to learn more, take the next step, or receive a free Quran?
whatIsIslam.faqQ1: What does the word Islam mean?
whatIsIslam.faqA1: Islam means peace attained through willing submission to God. It comes from the Arabic root s-l-m (peace, safety, submission). A Muslim is someone who submits to the one God, Allah.
whatIsIslam.faqA2: Muslims worship God alone — called Allah in Arabic — the one Creator of everything. They do not worship the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, any human being, idols or images.
whatIsIslam.faqQ3: Is Islam connected to Christianity and Judaism?
whatIsIslam.faqA3: Yes. Muslims believe Islam is the same core message brought by all the prophets, including Abraham, Moses and Jesus — to worship the one God and live righteously.
whatIsIslam.faqQ4: How does someone become a Muslim?
whatIsIslam.faqA4: A person becomes Muslim by sincerely declaring the Shahada: that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah, and that Muhammad ﷺ is His messenger. No ceremony or permission is required.

fivePillars.title: The Five Pillars of Islam
fivePillars.intro: The five pillars are the foundation of a Muslim's life — five acts of worship that every Muslim strives to fulfil. Together they connect belief with daily practice, balancing devotion to God with generosity and self-discipline.
fivePillars.shahadaText: The Shahada is the testimony that there is no god worthy of worship except God (Allah), and that Muhammad ﷺ is His messenger. Sincerely declaring it is how a person enters Islam, and it is repeated daily in prayer.
fivePillars.salahText: Muslims pray five times a day — at dawn, midday, afternoon, sunset and night — facing the Kaaba in Mecca. Salah is a direct connection between the worshipper and God, a recurring moment of focus and gratitude woven through the day.
fivePillars.zakatText: Zakat is an annual obligation to give a small portion (usually 2.5%) of one's accumulated wealth to those in need. It purifies wealth, reduces inequality, and reminds Muslims that everything they own is a trust from God.
fivePillars.sawmText: During the month of Ramadan, Muslims fast from dawn to sunset, abstaining from food, drink and bad habits. Fasting builds self-discipline, empathy for those who go hungry, and a renewed closeness to God.
fivePillars.hajjText: Hajj is the pilgrimage to Mecca that every Muslim who is able must perform once in a lifetime. Millions gather each year in simple white garments, standing equal before God regardless of wealth or background.
fivePillars.ctaText: New to Islam, or want to learn how to pray? We are here to help.
fivePillars.faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions About the Five Pillars
fivePillars.faqQ1: How many pillars of Islam are there?
fivePillars.faqA1: There are five pillars of Islam: the declaration of faith (Shahada), prayer (Salah), charity (Zakat), fasting in Ramadan (Sawm) and pilgrimage to Mecca (Hajj).
fivePillars.faqQ2: What is the most important pillar of Islam?
fivePillars.faqA2: The Shahada — the declaration of faith — is the first and foundational pillar; a person enters Islam by sincerely declaring it. The other four pillars build on this belief.
fivePillars.faqQ3: Does every Muslim have to perform Hajj?
fivePillars.faqA3: Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime only for Muslims who are physically and financially able to make the journey. Those who genuinely cannot are not sinful for not performing it.
